Method of Attack: Hides in WordPress dashboard from users without specific User-Agent strings
Announces presence via GET requests with custom parameters (e.g., initiationactivity, testingkey)
Uploads arbitrary files including web shells and brute-force scripts via POST requests
Acts as backdoors to maintain access after original infection vector removal
Enables brute-force attacks on other websites
Some variants mine Bitcoin cryptocurrency using dedicated Linux binaries (64-bit and 32-bit)
Attack Vector: Fake WordPress plugins installed on compromised sites
Malicious payloads embedded in source code of legitimate plugins or created with automated tools
